Fulfil
fụl-fĭl´
v. (to fill full; to accomplish, bring to completion; rendering Hebrew male, Greek pleroo and anapleroo)
Old English fullfyllan, to fill full. The Greek pleroo keeps the picture: a thing fulfilled is a vessel filled to the brim, not a task crossed off.

Biblical Definition

The Lord of the law: “Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil” (Mat 5:17). At Jordan: “Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness” (Mat 3:15). Paul: “all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself” (Gal 5:14); “Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ” (Gal 6:2). To Archippus: “Take heed to the ministry which thou hast received in the Lord, that thou fulfil it” (Col 4:17). And the warning: “make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof” (Rom 13:14). In the Old Testament the word is God keeping a word: Solomon put out Abiathar “that he might fulfil the word of the LORD, which he spake concerning the house of Eli” (1Ki 2:27).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines fulfil as to accomplish; to perform; to complete; to answer in execution or event; to fill up.

expand to see more

FULFIL, v.t. To accomplish; to perform; to complete; to answer in execution or event what has been foretold or promised; as, to fulfil a prophecy or prediction.

2. To accomplish what was intended; to answer a design by execution.

3. To accomplish or perform what was desired; to answer any desire by compliance or gratification.

4. To perform what is required; to answer a law by obedience.

Key Scripture

Mat 5:17 — "Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil."

Mat 3:15 — "And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffered him."

Gal 5:14 — "For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself."

Gal 6:2 — "Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ."

Col 4:17 — "And say to Archippus, Take heed to the ministry which thou hast received in the Lord, that thou fulfil it."

Rom 13:14 — "But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof."

Modern Corruption

Fulfil is read as a polite word for abolish, and the Lord's next sentence says not one jot or tittle shall pass.

expand to see more

Matthew 5:17 is the hinge on which the whole question of the law turns, and it has been read as if fulfil meant finish off: Christ completed the law, therefore the Christian is done with it. The Lord anticipated the reading and closed it in the next two verses — till heaven and earth pass, not one jot or tittle shall pass from the law, and whosoever shall break one of these least commandments and teach men so shall be called least in the kingdom. To fulfil is to fill full: to bring the law to its complete expression in His teaching, its complete obedience in His life, and its complete satisfaction in His death. The Confession's word for what remains is the moral law doth for ever bind all, and Galatians 5:14 shows Paul, the apostle of grace, still measuring love by the law it fulfils.

Matthew 3:15 is the other half of the gospel. Christ was baptised, not for His own sins, but “to fulfil all righteousness” — to keep every requirement laid on a son of Israel, from the eighth day to the Jordan to the cross, so that a whole righteousness would exist in a Man and could be counted to men. The doctrine is called the active obedience of Christ, and it is why the believer is not merely pardoned but righteous: the law was not only satisfied on his behalf, it was fulfilled on his behalf. A religion that has Christ dying for us but not living for us has half a Saviour and a robe with no cloth in it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew male (H4390), to fill, be full, fulfil; Greek pleroo (G4137), to fill, make full, fulfil; anapleroo (G378), to fill up; teleo (G5055), to complete.

expand to see more

Hebrew male (H4390) — to fill, fulfil; Genesis 29:27, Exodus 23:26, 1 Kings 2:27, 2 Chronicles 36:21, Psalm 20:4–5.

Greek pleroo (G4137) — to fill full, fulfil; Matthew 3:15, 5:17, Galatians 5:14, Colossians 4:17, Philippians 2:2.

Greek anapleroo (G378) — to fill up; Galatians 6:2, 1 Thessalonians 2:16; teleo (G5055), James 2:8, “fulfil the royal law.”

Usage

"“I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil” — and not one jot shall pass."

"“Thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness” — the active obedience, begun at Jordan."

"“Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ” — the law kept by carrying."
